head.title: spaCR: spatial phenotype analysis of CRISPR-Cas9 screens
head.description: spaCR {{SPACR_VERSION}}: segmentation, single-cell measurement, classification, barcode mapping and regression for image-based pooled CRISPR screens. Pipeline, published models, screen results, papers and installation.
tabs.label: spaCR sections
overview.lede: Spatial phenotype analysis of CRISPR-Cas9 screens.
overview.prose: spaCR segments cells, nuclei and pathogens in microscopy images, measures every object, and links the measurements to the guide RNAs sequenced from the same wells. It starts from plate images and FASTQ reads and ends with per-cell measurements, trained classifiers and a ranked list of genes.

ov.flow.title: What spaCR does
ov.flow.intro: Seven modules, run in order. Each one reads the previous module's output and writes its own into the same project folder. Segmentation, measurement, annotation and classification also run without sequencing data.
ov.mod.import.name: Import
ov.mod.import.text: Converts microscope files into one folder layout per plate.
ov.mod.mask.name: Mask
ov.mod.mask.text: Segments cells, nuclei, parasites and organelles with Cellpose models.
ov.mod.measure.name: Measure
ov.mod.measure.text: Measures shape, intensity, texture and position of every object.
ov.mod.annotate.name: Annotate
ov.mod.annotate.text: Labels object crops in a keyboard-driven grid.
ov.mod.classify.name: Classify
ov.mod.classify.text: Trains image models (ResNet, MaxViT) or measurement models (XGBoost, random forest).
ov.mod.classify.out: Checkpoints with held-out metrics, per-object scores
ov.mod.barcodes.name: Map barcodes
ov.mod.barcodes.text: Decodes row, column and guide barcodes from FASTQ reads.
ov.mod.regression.name: Regression
ov.mod.regression.text: Estimates guide and gene effects from scores and guide counts.
ov.mod.regression.out: Volcano plot and ranked hit list
ov.mod.more.name: And more
ov.flow.more: Dose-response, control charts, plaque and recruitment assays, image UMAP, batch correction, power and plate design, and a QC dashboard. See Assays and QC and Phenotypes.

screen.title: Screen results
screen.intro: A pooled CRISPR screen in Toxoplasma gondii for parasite genes that affect recruitment of the host ESCRT protein GFP-TSG101 to the parasite vacuole, analysed with spaCR. From the spaCR preprint.
screen.stat.permgenes: genes past FDR 5% and the effect cut, by permutation
screen.perm.title: Permutation tests
screen.perm.intro: spaCR's guide-permutation analysis (Regression, nonparametric inference) on the screen's MaxViT per-cell scores: each gene's and each guide's partial correlation with the well-mean score, given plate, row and column, against 2,000,000 within-plate Freedman–Lane permutations (seed 0). Layout as in the preprint's Figure S7 (panels R and S). With the example's shipped settings, control wells and guides stay in, so the numbers differ from the preprint, which excluded them and filtered wells. Data: spacr-example-screen, settings from spacr-example-hit.
screen.perm.gene.alt: Gene-level permutation volcano: partial correlation against minus log10 BH-adjusted empirical P, coloured by compartment; GRA14, EAF1 and SAG1 named.
screen.perm.gene.caption: Gene level: 414 genes tested (each gene's summed guide fractions). 4 reach BH q < 0.05 (SAG1 (TGGT1_233460) r = −0.317, P = 5.0×10⁻⁷, q = 1.0×10⁻⁴; GRA14 (TGGT1_239740) r = +0.435, P = 5.0×10⁻⁷, q = 1.0×10⁻⁴; EAF1 (TGGT1_225160) r = +0.240, P = 1.0×10⁻⁶, q = 1.4×10⁻⁴; GRA12B (TGGT1_275860) r = +0.157, P = 1.7×10⁻⁴, q = 1.7×10⁻²); 3 also pass the effect cut: SAG1 (TGGT1_233460), GRA14 (TGGT1_239740), EAF1 (TGGT1_225160). 2 genes sit at the P floor (no permutation as extreme). 2,000,000 within-plate Freedman-Lane permutations, seed 0; smallest attainable P = 1/(B+1) = 5.0×10⁻⁷. MaxViT per-cell scores averaged per well, 1,290 wells on 4 plates, partial Pearson r given plate, row and column. Dashed line BH q = 0.05; dotted lines the spaCR effect cut (3x std of 29 controls = 0.221).
screen.perm.guide.alt: Guide-level permutation volcano: partial correlation against minus log10 BH-adjusted empirical P, coloured by compartment; GRA14 guides 1 and 3, SAG1 guide 4 and EAF1 guide 2 named.
screen.perm.guide.caption: Guide level: 953 guides tested. 3 reach BH q < 0.05 (SAG1 guide 4 r = −0.317, P = 5.0×10⁻⁷, q = 1.6×10⁻⁴; GRA14 guide 1 r = +0.397, P = 5.0×10⁻⁷, q = 1.6×10⁻⁴; GRA14 guide 3 r = +0.263, P = 5.0×10⁻⁷, q = 1.6×10⁻⁴); 3 pass the effect cut. 3 guides sit at the P floor. 2,000,000 within-plate Freedman-Lane permutations, seed 0; smallest attainable P = 1/(B+1) = 5.0×10⁻⁷. MaxViT per-cell scores averaged per well, 1,290 wells on 4 plates, partial Pearson r given plate, row and column. Dashed line BH q = 0.05; dotted lines the spaCR effect cut (3x std of 29 controls = 0.221).
screen.perm.null.alt: Three histograms of the permutation null of the partial correlation, for GRA14, EAF1 and SAG1, each with the observed value far outside the null.
screen.perm.null.caption: Permutation null of the gene-level partial correlation for GRA14, EAF1 and SAG1 (2,000,000 draws, seed 0; log count scale). Solid line: observed r; dashed: -r (the test is two-sided on |r|). b = permutations at least as extreme; P = (b+1)/(B+1). GRA14 r = +0.435, b = 0; EAF1 r = +0.240, b = 1; SAG1 r = −0.317, b = 0. The draws were regenerated from spaCR's own projection and seeded generator, and their exceedance counts equal the counts spaCR reported for these genes.
screen.ols.title: All four plates: gene effects from spaCR's OLS regression
screen.ols.hint: Hover or tab to a point for its values; click it, or press Enter, for the gene card. Arrow keys move between genes, Escape closes the card.
screen.ols.caption2: Ordinary least squares on the MaxViT per-cell scores of all four screen plates (1,290 wells, 414 genes, 953 guides), as spaCR's Regression module runs it on its test data. Height is the raw p; Benjamini–Hochberg FDR 5% decides the colour and the dashed line. Dotted lines: ±3σ (MAD) of the gene effects. 225160 (TGGT1_225160) is the gene the preprint names EAF1. Data: spacr-example-screen.
screen.ols.plot: Volcano plot of gene effects. Use the arrow keys to move between genes and Enter to open a gene card.
screen.ols.zeronote: (reported as 0; drawn three decades above the smallest non-zero p, as spaCR does)
screen.ols.card.controlnote: Non-targeting guides, not a gene: the null this screen measures every real guide against.
screen.ols.error: The regression results could not be loaded.
phenotypes.title: Phenotypes
phenotypes.intro: Every measured cell can be placed on a two-dimensional map with its image crop, so that groups of similar cells can be found and checked by eye.
phenotypes.umap.alt2: UMAP scatter of 5,000 cells forming 6 outlined, numbered clusters on the left; on the right one row per cluster with its number, its cell count and four example single-cell crops framed in the cluster colour.
phenotypes.umap.caption2: UMAP of 6 measurements of 5,000 randomly sampled cells from screen plate 1 (60,816 cells), 6 DBSCAN clusters that differ mainly in nuclei and parasite objects per cell (1: 2,529 cells, median 1 nucleus and 1 parasite object; 2: 146 cells, median 1 nucleus and 1 parasite object; 3: 1,131 cells, median 1 nucleus and 2 parasite objects; 4: 468 cells, median 2 nuclei and 1 parasite object; 5: 502 cells, median 2 nuclei and 3 parasite objects; 6: 223 cells, median 3 nuclei and 3 parasite objects); crops are cells near each cluster centre.
phenotypes.cls.title: Classification
phenotypes.cls.intro: Classifiers that tell the screen's control wells apart, trained and explained with spaCR on CPU: an XGBoost model on per-cell measurements and a small image model (MobileNetV3-small, 8 epochs) on single-cell crops. Column 1 wells carry guides against SAG1 (negative control) and column 2 wells against GRA14 (positive control). Wells are held out whole, so no test cell shares a well with a training cell. Data: spacr-example-screen and spacr-example-hit, plate 1, CC BY 4.0.
phenotypes.cls.crops.alt2: Two three-by-three grids of single-cell fluorescence crops on black, labelled SAG1 (left) and GRA14 (right). Each crop shows a HeLa cell with a blue nucleus, green GFP-TSG101 and red Toxoplasma vacuoles; in most SAG1 crops the vacuoles look yellow where green overlaps red, in the GRA14 crops they stay red.
phenotypes.cls.crops.caption2: The 9 held-out cells per class that spaCR's CNN classified correctly with the highest confidence, from 405 test cells (306 SAG1-well, 99 GRA14-well) in 4 wells never used for training (A01, C02, F01, H01); test accuracy 0.909, ROC AUC 0.958.
phenotypes.cls.saliency.alt2: Four rows of five single-cell crops: SAG1 crops, the same cells as dim grey images with a magma heat overlay of input-gradient saliency drawn only inside the cell, then GRA14 crops and their saliency overlays. The heat is brightest along the cell outline, with smaller hot spots inside the cells.
phenotypes.cls.saliency.caption2: Input-gradient saliency (SmoothGrad, 32 samples) of the CNN for the 5 most confident correct held-out cells per class, shown inside the cell only; in 10 of 10 cells the share of saliency inside the cell (39-93%) is below the share of the crop the cell covers (50-95%), and inside the cell it peaks at the cell outline.
phenotypes.cls.shap.alt: SHAP beeswarm: twelve feature names on the left, one row of coloured dots per feature along a horizontal SHAP value axis from about -1.1 to 1.4. The top rows, cell_channel_1_shannon_entropy and cell_channel_1_channel_2_M2_correlation_85, spread widest in both directions; lower rows cluster near zero.
phenotypes.cls.shap.caption2: SHAP values of spaCR's XGBoost model for 256 held-out cells from 3 wells (C02, D02, H01), top 12 of 76 features by mean |SHAP|; each dot is a cell coloured by its feature value (dark low, yellow high), and positive values push toward the GRA14 class (well-grouped 5-fold accuracy 0.853, ROC AUC 0.922 on 1,277 cells).
phenotypes.cls.shapcell.alt2: SHAP waterfall for one cell: ten horizontal arrows, red pushing right and blue pushing left, from the expected value 0.178 at the bottom to f(x) = 1.545 at the top; cell_channel_1_shannon_entropy adds the largest positive contribution.
phenotypes.cls.shapcell.caption2: Per-cell SHAP explanation of one held-out GRA14-well cell (plate 1, well C02, field 1, object 35): the model's base value of 0.178 log-odds plus the feature contributions gives 1.545, a GRA14 probability of 0.82.
phenotypes.cls.importance.alt2: Horizontal grey bar chart of the 15 most important measurement features, longest bar at the top for cell_channel_1_channel_2_M2_correlation_85 (about 0.20), then cell_channel_1_shannon_entropy (about 0.13).
phenotypes.cls.importance.caption: Top 15 of 76 features by XGBoost importance for the model trained on 1,021 control cells from 13 wells; cell_channel_1_channel_2_M2_correlation_85 ranks first (0.196), then cell_channel_1_shannon_entropy (0.133).

about.title: About
about.intro: This site presents spaCR and related microscopy projects: software, segmentation models and hardware, with the data and code behind each figure.
about.affiliation_text: Research Investigator, Department of Microbiology & Immunology, University of Michigan
about.bio_text: Einar B. Olafsson is a Research Investigator in the Department of Microbiology & Immunology at the University of Michigan. He studies how Toxoplasma gondii interacts with the cells it infects, combining CRISPR screening, high-content microscopy and AI-based single-cell image analysis to link genetic perturbations to spatial cellular phenotypes. He created and maintains spaCR. He studied biology and immunology at Uppsala University and received his PhD in Molecular Biosciences from Stockholm University, with a thesis on signalling in Toxoplasma dissemination by infected immune cells.
